synthetic-solo-one-voice-20200101-000001.title: Synthetic — one voice, long turns
synthetic-solo-one-voice-20200101-000001.note: The trivial positive control: one speaker, nothing to separate.

synthetic-two-long-turns-20200101-000002.title: Synthetic — two voices, long turns
synthetic-two-long-turns-20200101-000002.note: Two genuine speakers taking long turns — the easiest case for a coherence metric, and the shape the only pre-existing positive control had.

synthetic-two-medium-turns-20200101-0000.title: Synthetic — two voices, five-second turns
synthetic-two-medium-turns-20200101-0000.note: Two genuine speakers at 5 s a turn — the middle of the bracket around the 0.30 fragmentation gate.

synthetic-two-rapid-alternation-20200101.title: Synthetic — two voices, rapid alternation
synthetic-two-rapid-alternation-20200101.note: Two genuine speakers swapping every ~3 s. Named by docs/COUNT_ESTIMATION_DESIGN.md as the case the fragmentation rule was never tested against: a real speaker here produces many short runs, which is what the rule reads as a phantom. This fixture is the counter-example — its speaker count is KNOWN to be 2.

synthetic-two-backchannel-20200101-00000.title: Synthetic — two voices, one only backchannels
synthetic-two-backchannel-20200101-00000.note: A genuine second speaker who only ever says 'mm-hm' and 'right'. Low duration ratio, and the interjections are spread through the whole meeting — the quiet-but-real participant the duration gate is supposed to protect.

synthetic-four-voices-20200101-000006.title: Synthetic — four voices
synthetic-four-voices-20200101-000006.note: Four genuine speakers — the counter-direction control: whatever folds phantoms must leave these four apart.

synthetic-same-voice-drift-20200101-0000.title: Synthetic — one voice that drifts
synthetic-same-voice-drift-20200101-0000.note: ONE person whose embeddings rotate 80 degrees across the meeting. The ends are further apart than the clustering threshold, but the halves' centroids are close enough that _fold_weak_clusters merges them. Must not be two people.

synthetic-same-voice-split-20200101-0000.title: Synthetic — one voice with a scattered second lobe
synthetic-same-voice-split-20200101-0000.note: ONE person, 12% of whose windows sit 0.65 away from their own centroid, scattered so they land in runs of one. Reproduces the real-corpus phantom: the split survives BOTH folds, so the auto path returns 2 clusters for 1 person. Anything that counts clusters gets this wrong.

synthetic-same-voice-big-split-20200101-.title: Synthetic — one voice with a large scattered second lobe
synthetic-same-voice-big-split-20200101-.note: The same one person, but with a lobe big enough that the runner-up carries ~40% of the dominant cluster's speech. Still one person. Included because it is the case a duration test alone cannot reject — only the scatter distinguishes it.

synthetic-call-clean-audio-20200101-0000.title: Synthetic — online call, call audio captured
synthetic-call-clean-audio-20200101-0000.note: System/mic speech ratio ~0.97. The fallback must never fire.

synthetic-call-half-volume-20200101-0000.title: Synthetic — online call, far end talks half as much

synthetic-call-third-volume-20200101-000.title: Synthetic — online call, far end talks a third as much

synthetic-call-brief-far-end-20200101-00.title: Synthetic — online call, far end barely speaks
synthetic-call-brief-far-end-20200101-00.note: System/mic ratio ~0.11 — well under any plausible ratio gate, and still a call whose audio was captured perfectly.

synthetic-call-quiet-far-end-20200101-00.title: Synthetic — online call, quietest far end in the corpus
synthetic-call-quiet-far-end-20200101-00.note: System/mic ratio ~0.03, and its shortest single segment is ~1 s against 96 s of mic. This is the fixture the absolute-vs-ratio check is aimed at: a ratio gate fires here, an absolute one cannot.

synthetic-ask-demo-call-20200101-000020.title: Synthetic — processed call with colliding turn starts
synthetic-ask-demo-call-20200101-000020.note: Already-labelled meeting used by the citation tests: two turns start at exactly 0.00 and two more pairs 0.30 s apart, so a cited timestamp cannot choose between them.
